title: Local sheafified derived Hom, cohomological boundaries and lower amplitude
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings, using [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(\mathcal O)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with standard cohomology [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and use derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and put $T^n(M)=H^nR\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,M)$. For an object $U$ let $\mathcal O_U$ and $M|_U$ denote restriction to the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Then:

1. For every integer $n$ there is an isomorphism of module sheaves
$$T^n(M)\cong\bigl(U\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,M|_U[n])\bigr)^\#,$$
where $\#$ is module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the module action is postcomposition with multiplication by sections of $\mathcal O$, and restriction on the presheaf is induced by derived restriction and its canonical composition comparisons. The isomorphism is additive, natural in $M$, and compatible with restriction in $U$; for complexes $P,I$ representing $K,M$ with $I$ K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pur-hom-complex] it sends a Hom-complex degree-$n$ cocycle to its localized derived morphism $P|_U\to I|_U[n]$.
2. Each $T^n$ is additive. A distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ gives a natural long exact sequence of module sheaves $\cdots\to T^n(X)\to T^n(Y)\to T^n(Z)\to T^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$. Under (1) the boundary is induced by local postcomposition with $w[n]$. These sequences and the identifications $T^n(M[t])\cong T^{n+t}(M)$ are coherent with shifts and natural in triangle morphisms; in particular $T^0$ is homological [def-sp-homological-functor].
3. For all integers $r,b$, if $H^j(K)=0$ for $j>r$ and $H^j(M)=0$ for $j<b$, then $T^n(M)=0$ for $n<b-r$. No finite Tor amplitude or bound on site cohomological dimension is required.

proof.text: Let rho be the target-shift presheaf comparison. Define d as P_n applied to the triangle last arrow followed by rho_(1,n). The local formula follows from naturality and the section formula for rho. Sheafification compatibility follows by naturality of sigma and tau and the sheafification equation for rho. This works for every triangle and in particular every distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Exact restriction preserves the standard t-structure bounds. If K is at most r and M is at least b, the restrictions of K and M[n] are in degrees at most r and at least b-n. For n<b-r orthogonality makes every local Hom zero. Section equivalence makes the cohomology presheaf zero, and its sheafification is T_n(M), so T_n(M) is zero.
